Supplementary results (S11) containing the explicit bvFTD-versus-control peak coordinates are not included in the provided main text but are indicated as present in the Supplement; missing supplementary material is acceptable per screening instructions. Therefore, I include the study but note moderate confidence because the explicit bvFTD-vs-control peak coordinates are not visible in the supplied main text.

The study uses VBM and includes an FTD patient subgroup (n=11) and healthy controls (n=22), but it does not present any whole-brain, voxelwise contrast that isolates a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) group versus controls with reported peak coordinates. The VBM analyses reported are correlations across a heterogeneous sample (multiple diagnoses) relating atrophy to Flanker task performance, not bvFTD-versus-control group contrasts, and no MNI/Talairach peak coordinates for a bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrast are provided. Therefore the paper meets I3 (VBM) and I5 (>=6 patients in a patient group), but fails I4 (explicit bvFTD sample/labeling for the reported contrasts), I6 (bvFTD vs control between-group contrast not reported), I7 (no whole-brain group-level result clearly identified as from the target bvFTD sample), and I8 (no peak coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control contrast). Full text appears complete. Excluded on these grounds.

Exclusion E6 applies: the VBM results reported for the overeating FTD patients were assessed within a predefined a-priori ROI and significance was accepted at p<0.05 corrected within that ROI. The paper does not present an unrestricted whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrast (whole-brain corrected) for the bvFTD/binge-eating FTD group versus controls, so it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I7) and therefore must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinical FTD patients with behavioral syndrome described), I5 (patient group n=6 and controls n=47), I6 (between-group contrast of overeating FTD patients vs controls reported), and I8 (peak coordinates are reported for key effects). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no clearly reported whole-brain, voxelwise group-level result for the target bvFTD group). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion provided).

The study uses FDG-PET and includes 11 FTLD patients, but it does not specifically state inclusion of clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick's disease cases, and the reported imaging results are region-based (z-scores across predefined ROIs) and descriptive regional hypometabolism rather than whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts with stereotactic peak coordinates. Therefore it fails critical inclusion criteria requiring (I4) explicit bvFTD/Pick cases, (I6) a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast, (I7) whole-brain voxelwise group-level results, and (I8) reported peak coordinates. It also meets exclusion criterion E6 because the qualifying imaging results are ROI-based and no unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates are provided. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports group-level contrasts of an FTD patient subgroup (ALS-FTD) versus neurologic controls. The ALS-FTD subgroup (n = 18) meets the minimum sample size requirement and is described using Neary criteria with prominent behavioral abnormalities consistent with behavioral-variant FTD; the control group (n = 15) also meets the minimum. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM results comparing ALS-FTD to controls and indicates MNI coordinates are provided in the paper’s tables for peak voxels. The ALS-FTD group is presented as a distinct patient group (not pooled) in these contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (comorbidity with ALS is acceptable per review rules).

This FDG-PET study clearly targets bvFTD and meets multiple inclusion requirements: it uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed and pathology-confirmed bvFTD patients (I4), has adequate patient and control group sizes (I5), reports group-level voxelwise analyses in MNI space comparing bvFTD vs controls (I6,I7). However, the paper does not report any explicit peak coordinates (x,y,z) for whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control contrasts; results are described as regional topographies and thresholded images without peak coordinate tables or coordinate values. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I8 (coordinates must exist) required for coordinate-based meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion E7 applies: the paper does not provide a clinically defined bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) group separate from other diagnoses. The FTLD group is mixed (FTD N=3, SD N=6, mixed N=4) and any bvFTD/FTD cases are few and not reported as a standalone bvFTD-versus-control contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no distinct clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick's disease sample reported), I5 (bvFTD patient group <6 or not separable), I6 (no between-group bvFTD vs control contrast reported), I7 (no whole-brain group-level result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target group), I8 (no peak coordinates reported for a bvFTD-versus-control contrast). Therefore the study does not meet the review’s requirements for inclusion.

Although this study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and included a clinically diagnosed FTD variant group with sufficient sample size, it does not report a whole-brain, between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD/FTD group against healthy controls with peak coordinates. The paper's imaging analyses are trait-wise VBM correlations across a mixed diagnostic sample and co-atrophy checks controlling for diagnosis; it does not present a bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise contrast in MNI/Talairach space with reported peak (x,y,z) coordinates. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I8. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM imaging), I4 (FTD patients included), I5 (sample sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no explicit bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrast), I7 (no group-level whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group), I8 (no reported peak coordinates for a bvFTD-vs-control whole-brain contrast in the provided text). No exclusion criteria from the list apply.

This full-text empirical VBM study clearly meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses voxel-based morphometry for whole-brain analyses; (I4) includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=13); (I5) sample sizes meet thresholds (bvFTD=13, controls=12); (I6) reports between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD versus controls (VBM t-tests described); (I7) whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results are reported; (I8) peak coordinates in MNI space are provided (e.g., MNI Coordinates: x=14, y=-4, z=-16) and methods state MNI stereotaxic reporting. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore include for meta-analysis.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=18) and uses 18F-FDG PET, and includes an adequate control group (n=29), it does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing the bvFTD group to controls in standard stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach). The PET analyses described are voxel-wise regressions of metabolism against oculomotor parameters conducted across the patient sample (no controls in the PET subset) and report anatomical regions (e.g., right middle frontal gyrus, precuneus) but do not provide peak coordinates (x,y,z) for any bvFTD-versus-control contrast. Therefore the paper fails inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered by the available full text. Full text appears complete for assessment.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare a clinically defined behavioral FTD sample against healthy controls, reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts, and provides stereotactic coordinates in the text (e.g., voxel coordinates (0, −28, −10) used to define the periaqueductal gray sphere). Sample sizes meet thresholds (9 FTD, 26 controls). Whole-brain VBM results (P<0.05 corrected) are reported for multiple rostral limbic system regions; SVC was additionally used for the periaqueductal gray. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Note: peak-coordinate reporting in tables/figures is not present in the provided text excerpt beyond the one coordinate, but a stereotactic coordinate is given in the methods, supporting spatial reporting.

Imaging modality and sample: The study uses resting-state fMRI (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases within the cohort (bvFTD-only N=3; bvFTD+ [bvFTD or ALS-FTD] N=9) fulfilling the sample requirement (I4) and having >=6 patients in the bvFTD+ subgroup and controls (I5). However, the paper does NOT report any bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (the reported comparisons are: all C9+ vs HC, and bvFTD+ vs ALS-only) so I6 is not met. The analysis is based on parcellated ROI time series (82 VOIs) and graph-theory/edge analyses rather than unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise results; no peak coordinates (MNI/Talairach) are provided (I7 and I8 not met). Because the qualifying results derive from region-based/parcellation analyses and no unrestricted voxelwise contrasts or coordinates are reported, exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain voxelwise report) applies. Therefore the study is excluded.

This full text reports whole-brain VBM analyses including a clearly defined bvFTLD (behavioral/dysexecutive) subgroup (bvFTLD; n=71 overall, imaging subset n=51) and comparisons against an age-matched control cohort (~42–43 controls). The methods describe voxelwise, whole-brain VBM contrasts in MNI space with statistical thresholds, and the manuscript reports peak coordinates for atrophic clusters for bvFTLD versus controls (tables referenced). Thus the study meets imaging modality (I3: VBM), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), has sufficient sample sizes for patient and control groups (I5), reports between-group voxelwise contrasts for bvFTLD versus controls (I6), provides whole-brain group-level voxelwise results from the target sample (I7), and reports peak coordinates for those contrasts (I8). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets several inclusion criteria: I3 (voxelwise gray-matter analysis using VBM-like pipeline/voxelwise two-sample t-test), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (patient and control group sizes meet minimums; N=16 bvFTD, N=16 controls for behavior; MRI subset N=11 bvFTD and N=14 controls), and I6/I7 (reports whole-brain, group-level bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise contrasts with FDR correction and cluster thresholds). However, the provided full text does NOT report any peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach) for the whole-brain bvFTD>control or control>bvFTD contrasts; tables/figures are referenced but no numeric peak coordinates appear in the supplied content. Therefore inclusion criterion I8 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Full text appears complete for core sections (intro, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Excluded because I8 (reporting of peak coordinates) is not met, preventing inclusion in the coordinate-based meta-analysis.

Although this study uses VBM (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed FTD (bvFTD-like) subgroup (Neary FTD variant) with adequate sample size (30 patients; I4 and I5), it does NOT report a between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast of the bvFTD group versus healthy controls. The authors explicitly state that normal controls were not used in any VBM analysis, and the reported voxelwise results are correlational analyses across a mixed diagnostic sample and subgroup empathy-related interactions, not a direct bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain comparison. Consequently the paper fails to meet I6 (between-group bvFTD vs controls), I7 (a whole-brain group-level result coming from the target sample), and I8 (peak coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This task-based fMRI study includes 7 FTD patients and reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM results with Talairach peak coordinates (supplementary tables) for FTD vs AD contrasts. However, it does not explicitly specify that the FTD sample is behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease, nor does it present a bvFTD-versus-healthy-control whole-brain contrast. Key inclusion criteria unmet: no explicit bvFTD labeling (I4), no bvFTD vs control between-group contrast reported (I6), and therefore no bvFTD-versus-control peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (I8). It does meet that it used task-based fMRI (I3), had >=6 patients in the patient group (I5), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results for the FTD sample (I7). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

Although this study uses VBM (I3) and includes sufficient sample sizes (FTD n=29; controls n=12) satisfying I5, and the FTD sample contains a subgroup described as having social/executive dysfunction consistent with bvFTD (I4), the paper reports results for a combined FTD group rather than a separately analyzed bvFTD (behavioral-variant) subgroup. The manuscript does not present a bvFTD-specific whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast against controls nor does it report peak coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control contrast. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I8 required for this review. Full text appears complete for core sections. Excluded for not providing bvFTD-specific whole-brain coordinate results.

Full text reports VBM analysis in a cohort including 31 bvFTD patients vs. 56 controls and whole-brain VBM contrasts, satisfying imaging modality and group/contrast criteria. However, no peak coordinates (MNI/Talairach x,y,z) are present in the provided full text; they are likely in Table S2 / Supporting Information which is not included here. Because the paper as provided does not allow verification of reported peak coordinates required by I8, I must exclude the study pending access to the supplementary material. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met.

The study includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=41) and healthy controls (n=56) and uses structural MRI with voxelwise gray-matter probability maps (VBM-like), satisfying I4 and I5 and I3. However, it does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls, nor does it provide peak coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control contrast. Instead, the paper reports multivariate SCCAN correlations across a heterogeneous sample and PBAC-derived networks; these are not group-level, whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control contrasts in MNI/Talairach space with peak coordinates. Therefore I6, I7, and I8 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Because required between-group voxelwise contrasts and coordinates for bvFTD versus controls are absent, the study must be excluded.

No between-group bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast with reported peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD patients included), I5 (bvFTD n=10; controls n=20). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reported bvFTD vs control between-group contrast in stereotactic space—analyses reported are correlations within combined FTLD and trait-correlates; subgroup contrasts vs controls are not presented as between-group contrasts), I7 (no clear whole-brain group-level voxelwise result identified specifically from the bvFTD group versus controls), I8 (no peak coordinates provided for any bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast). No exclusion criteria from E5–E9 apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study should be excluded because, although it meets some inclusion criteria, it does not report the required whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise contrasts or peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (used voxel-based morphometry/voxel-based morphometry analyses are described), I4 (included clinically diagnosed FTD patients with a social/executive subgroup corresponding to bvFTD), I5 (>=6 patients in patient group and >=6 controls in overall sample). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no between-group bvFTD vs control voxelwise contrast is reported; analyses are within-patient correlations of CSF tau with atrophy), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result identified as a bvFTD-versus-control contrast), I8 (no peak coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control contrast are provided in the provided text; Table 4/Figures referenced but coordinates not shown). No exclusion criteria from the list are explicitly met. Full text appears complete for narrative content but does not supply the required between-group VBM coordinates for inclusion.

The study used VBM (I3), included a clinically-diagnosed FTD group consistent with behavioral-variant features (I4), and had sufficient sample sizes in imaging subset (FTD n=6, controls n=13) meeting I5. However, it did not report any between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing a bvFTD (FTD) group versus controls; instead VBM analyses were regression correlations collapsed across groups. Therefore it fails I6, I7, and I8 (no bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise contrasts and no reported peak coordinates for such contrasts). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were met. Full text appears complete. Excluded because required between-group bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates were not reported.

Full text appears to be only an abstract and key methodological details needed for this review are missing (fulltext_incomplete=true). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (sample size: 29 FTD patients). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality not clearly one of VBM, fMRI, or explicitly FDG-PET; study reports SPECT and PET but does not specify FDG), I4 (unclear whether sample is specifically behavioral-variant FTD/bvFTD or mixed FTD subtypes), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast reported in defined stereotactic space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results clearly reported for the target sample), I8 (no peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space are reported). No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) are explicitly met. Because essential imaging/result details and coordinates are not present in the provided content and the full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded for this meta-analysis.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes adequate patient group sizes, but it does not provide the required bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrasts or peak coordinates in the provided full text. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used) and I5 (each patient group >=6; FTLD-T n=6, FTLD-U n=8; controls n=61). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not clearly report a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease group for the reported voxelwise contrasts — patients are grouped by pathology FTLD-T and FTLD-U), I6 (no between-group contrast reported that compares a bvFTD group to controls), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result reported for a bvFTD clinical group), I8 (no peak coordinates (x,y,z) are provided in the text supplied). Exclusion criteria met: E7 (bvFTD cases are not separable in the reported contrasts; the analyses are on pathologically-defined FTLD subtypes, not a clinically-defined bvFTD group). Additionally, the provided full text appears incomplete with respect to coordinate tables/complete group definitions (fulltext_incomplete=true). Given these deficits, the paper cannot be included for the bvFTD meta-analysis.

The study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on a clinically diagnosed FTD sample (n=18) with age-matched controls (n=17), and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM results and peak coordinates for correlational analyses. However, it does not present a between-group whole-brain contrast specifically comparing a behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD / frontal-variant FTD) subgroup versus controls (bvFTD cases are mixed with semantic dementia cases and no bvFTD-specific vs control contrast or peak coordinates for such a contrast are reported). Therefore it fails key criteria required for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This study used structural regional volumetry (manual/semiautomated VOIs) of striatum and thalamus in 21 FTD patients and tested VOI differences with t-tests. It does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). It does include >=6 patients (I5 met). The paper reports region-of-interest VOI analyses only and does not report any whole-brain voxelwise group results or peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (I6, I7, I8 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (results come from ROI analyses with no unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Exclusion IDs met: E6. Inclusion IDs met: I5. Inclusion IDs not met: I3, I4 (bvFTD specifically not confirmed), I6, I7, I8.

Excluded because the reported patient contrast is for an ALS/FTLD mixed group rather than a clinically defined bvFTD group; therefore the bvFTD cases are not separable in the reported contrasts (exclusion E7). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used) and I5 (sample sizes: 10 patients in patient group, 22 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no standalone bvFTD/bvFTD-only patient group contrast), I6 (no between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls), I7 (no whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only target sample), and I8 (no peak coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control contrast are provided in the supplied text). Additionally, the provided full text appears to lack the tables/peak-coordinate listings referenced (tables 2/3 and figure captions), so fulltext_incomplete=true; key information necessary to reassess inclusion (e.g., whether coordinates exist in tables or whether a bvFTD-only subgroup analysis was reported) is missing.

Excluded because the paper does not present a whole-brain, voxelwise bvFTD-versus-control between-group contrast with peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD with a behavioral/bvFTD subgroup), I5 (>=6 patients and >=6 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no bvFTD-only vs control between-group contrast reported; the reported patient-vs-control contrast pools all FTD subtypes), I7 (no whole-brain group-level result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only target sample), I8 (no peak coordinates reported for a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This article is a narrative review (non-empirical) summarizing MRI and PET applications in dementia rather than an original empirical study. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E5 (review/meta-analysis/narrative review) and E8 (non-empirical paper without original data). (b) Inclusion IDs met: none. (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (does not present original VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET data from the authors), I4 (no bvFTD/Pick patient sample reported), I5 (no patient or control group sizes reported or original sample with ≥6 participants), I6 (no between-group whole-brain contrast comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from target sample), I8 (no peak coordinates reported). Full text appears to be a complete narrative review, not an empirical report; therefore it cannot provide the primary, coordinate-based whole-brain contrasts required by the review objective.

This study used FDG-PET and included 8 clinically diagnosed FTD patients (satisfying I3 and I5). However, it does not specify that the sample is behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not met). Crucially, the paper does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts of a bvFTD group versus controls in stereotactic space, nor does it provide whole-brain group-level voxelwise results or peak coordinates (I6, I7, I8 not met). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore it cannot be included for the meta-analysis that requires whole-brain, coordinate-based bvFTD versus control contrasts.

The study is excluded because it does not meet required imaging and reporting criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed FTD sample) and I5 (patient group N=74 ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (uses SPECT, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrast vs. healthy controls reported), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results), and I8 (no peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) explicitly apply. The full text is complete and provides methods/results, but the imaging modality and lack of voxelwise, coordinate-based bvFTD-versus-control contrasts prevent inclusion in this meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it does not report any between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing the bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space, nor does it provide peak coordinates. It uses VBM as an imaging modality and reports classification sensitivities (DSI) based on automated MRI quantification, but results are presented as classifier performance rather than voxelwise group contrasts or coordinate tables. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (patient group N=50). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast in defined stereotactic space reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result identified from the target bvFTD sample), I8 (no peak coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain group-level VBM comparisons and regressions relating the SOC/EXEC (a behavioral-variant–like FTD subgroup) patient group (n=12) to healthy controls (n=12). However, the full text does not report any peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach space) for the between-group or regression VBM results; only anatomical regions, Brodmann areas and p-values/cluster sizes are given. Thus inclusion criterion I8 (reporting peak coordinates) is not met. All other applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete. Exclusion reason: missing reported coordinates required by I8.

Although this paper used whole-brain VBM (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients in its sample (I4), and had sufficient group sizes (PGRN+ n=8, PGRN- n=8, controls matched) meeting the minimum N>=6 requirement (I5), it does NOT provide the required bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast nor peak coordinates for a bvFTD-only group. The reported between-group contrasts are PGRN(+) vs controls and PGRN(−) vs controls (disease groups that include mixed clinical diagnoses) rather than an explicitly defined bvFTD group contrast (violates I6 and I7). Crucially, the paper does not report any peak (x,y,z) coordinates in MNI/Talairach space for a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast (violates I8). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are directly met. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet the key inclusion requirements I6 and I8 (and I7 in the sense of target-sample whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study includes FDG-PET and MRI and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses of FTLD versus controls, but it does not specify that the patient group is behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (it uses the broader FTLD label and does not separate bvFTD cases). Crucially, the paper does not report peak coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for any bvFTD-versus-control contrast; no bvFTD-specific voxelwise contrasts or coordinates are provided. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 (bvFTD/Pick’s diagnosis not demonstrated) and I8 (no peak coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast). I3 (uses FDG-PET) is satisfied, and the paper likely meets I5 (sample sizes appear >6), but the absence of a clearly identified bvFTD group and lack of coordinates means it cannot be included. Exclusion criterion E7 applies because bvFTD cases are not separable/identified within the reported FTLD group. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I6, I7, I8.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes an FTD subgroup ('NON-APH') characterized by social/behavioural and executive impairment consistent with behavioral-variant FTD. The paper uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD-like subgroup (I4) with n=14 and healthy controls n=12 meeting sample-size thresholds (I5). It reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM contrasts for FTD subgroups versus controls, normalized to Talairach space (methods state Talairach/Tournoux normalization) and references Tables (Tables 3–5) that summarize peak foci and between-group contrasts, indicating reported peak coordinates (I6–I8). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply.

This study should be excluded. Exclusion criteria met: E9 (study reports cortical thickness and surface-based morphometry/fractal dimension measures rather than the required modalities). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases; 8 bvFTD reported) and I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is surface-based morphometry/fractal dimension, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET), I6 (no peak coordinates reported for a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast in MNI/Talairach space in the provided full text), I7 (results are vertex-wise surface analyses rather than voxelwise whole-brain contrasts reported with standard stereotactic coordinates), and I8 (no peak x,y,z coordinates provided). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, and discussion).

Exclusion applied: E6 (results derive from ROI-based FreeSurfer volumetry, not an unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise analysis). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (imaging modality: study used ROI structural MRI volumes rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I4 (sample: no clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick's disease patients — primary sample is mild Alzheimer’s disease), I5 (bvFTD-specific sample size not met — although n=57 overall, these are AD patients, not bvFTD), I6 (no between-group bvFTD-versus-control contrast reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from a bvFTD sample), I8 (no peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach reported for any bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not address the review objective and must be excluded.

Although the study uses VBM (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) (I4) with adequate sample sizes for patients and MRI controls (I5), and reports bvFTD-versus-control contrasts in SPM (I6), the bvFTD results are reported only as ROI / small-volume-corrected findings. There is no clearly reported whole-brain, unrestricted voxelwise bvFTD-versus-control group result with peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. The only whole-brain two-sample test reported pooled all FTD patients versus controls, not bvFTD alone, and peak coordinates for bvFTD whole-brain contrasts are not provided. Therefore this paper meets exclusion criterion E6 (qualifying results come from ROI/SVC analyses only). Inclusion criteria I7 and I8 (a group-level whole-brain voxelwise result for the target group, and reported peak coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast) are not met. Accordingly the study must be excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality criterion required by the review: it uses 99mTc-ECD SPECT rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). While the sample includes clinically diagnosed frontal variant FTD (fvFTD/bvFTD cases) (I4 met) and group sizes meet the minimum (48 patients, 15 controls) (I5 met), the paper does not report a clear whole-brain, bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise contrast with peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (I6, I7, I8 not met). No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Although the study uses voxel-based morphometry (I3) and has adequate sample sizes (FTLD N=18; controls N=40) (I5), and the abstract reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons (suggesting I7), the available content does NOT permit verification that the FTLD sample specifically corresponds to clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease (I4). Crucially, the paper as provided does not report peak coordinates for any bvFTD/FTLD-versus-control whole-brain contrast (I8) nor allow confirmation that bvFTD cases are not pooled with other patient groups in reported contrasts (I6). Because the full text (methods/results/tables) is not available, essential inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) are clearly met based on the abstract alone. Request full text to reassess.

This study uses VBM (I3 satisfied), includes clinically characterised FTD patients with early prominent behavioural features (I4 satisfied) and has adequate sample sizes (16 patients, 9 controls; I5 satisfied). However, the paper does not present any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast of a bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) group vs healthy controls with reported peak coordinates. The analyses either compare the entire FTLD group to controls or report within-FTLD covariate analyses relating grey-matter to eating behaviours; bvFTD cases are not separable in a bvFTD-versus-control contrast. Therefore it fails I6, I7 and I8. Exclusion criterion E7 applies because a bvFTD-specific patient group/contrast is not separable in the reported results. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because no bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain voxelwise contrast with peak coordinates is reported (I6/I7/I8 not met; E7 met).

This article is a narrative review of PET approaches to dementia rather than an original empirical study reporting new subject-level imaging results. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (non-empirical paper/review). Inclusion criteria met: none. Specifically: I3 (modality) is not satisfied as the paper discusses FDG-PET but does not present an original study using VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET on a primary bvFTD/bvFTD-like sample; I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) is not met—while frontotemporal dementia is described generally, no bvFTD patient cohort is reported; I5 (>=6 patients) not met—no patient-group sizes reported for an original bvFTD cohort; I6/I7/I8 (between-group voxelwise contrasts, whole-brain group-level results, and reported peak coordinates) are not met—no primary voxelwise bvFTD-versus-control contrasts or coordinates are provided. Full text appears complete (not a truncated abstract). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis: it examines clinically diagnosed behavioral/ frontal-variant FTD patients and uses FDG-PET (I3, I4). The PET substudy includes 41 patients and 16 healthy controls, satisfying the minimum group sizes (I5). The authors report voxelwise, whole-brain SPM2 group contrasts comparing patient groups to controls and between haplotype-defined bvFTD subgroups (I6, I7). Peak coordinates are provided (Talairach coordinates for cluster maxima such as –48, 23, 32; 4, 36, –25, etc.), meeting the coordinate-reporting requirement (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion requirements: (I3) Voxel-based morphometry was used (Methods: FSL-VBM); (I4) Includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=15) recruited via clinic with consensus diagnosis; (I5) Sample sizes meet thresholds (bvFTD n=15; Controls n=20); (I6) Reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD (and AD) versus controls (whole-brain atrophy analyses); (I7) Provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the bvFTD group (VBM atrophy maps extracted with TFCE and FWE correction); (I8) States that maximum coordinates are provided in MNI stereotaxic space for significant clusters. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; no exclusion criteria apply. No ROI-only, non-empirical, or disallowed imaging methods were used.

The study uses FDG-PET and includes an FTD group (n=17), but it does not report analyses specific to clinically-diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) nor present any whole-brain, group-level voxelwise bvFTD-versus-control contrasts in MNI/Talairach space. No peak coordinates (x,y,z) are reported for any bvFTD-versus-control contrast. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria requiring (I4) explicit bvFTD/Pick's sample, (I6/I7) whole-brain group-level results from the target group, and (I8) peak coordinates. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded. It reports two case descriptions (plus CSF data in 7 other mutation carriers) and does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET whole-brain voxelwise analyses or provide any between-group bvFTD-vs-control contrasts with peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (the reported cases meet clinical bvFTD criteria). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modality VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET not used), I5 (patient group <6 participants), I6 (no between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result), I8 (no peak coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria IDs apply. Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Although the study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (Neary criteria) within its FTLD sample (I4) and has sufficient patient group size (14) (I5), it does not meet key review requirements. The reported contrasts compare a pooled FTLD group (FTD, SD, PPA) to an early-onset AD group (EOAD), not bvFTD versus healthy controls. The bvFTD cases are pooled with other FTLD subtypes and are not reported separately, so there is no bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain voxelwise contrast. Peak coordinates are reported for FTLD-versus-EOAD contrasts but not for any bvFTD-versus-control contrast. Therefore I6 (bvFTD vs controls contrast), I7 (whole-brain result from the target bvFTD sample), and I8 (peak coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control contrast) are not satisfied. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are directly met, but because required inclusion criteria are not all satisfied, the study must be excluded.

Inclusion met: I3 (the study uses voxel-based morphometry) and I5 (patient group FTLD n=55 and controls n=73, both ≥6). Inclusion not met: I4 (the sample does not present a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease group—FTLD is a pathologically defined umbrella and bvFTD is not specified/separated), I6/I7/I8 (the paper does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast or peak coordinates specifically for a bvFTD-versus-control comparison). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

This study investigates presymptomatic genetic mutation carriers versus familial controls rather than clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients. While it uses appropriate imaging modalities (resting-state fMRI and voxelwise grey/white matter density measures) and has sufficient group sizes (55 carriers, 48 controls), it does not report any between-group bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space nor provide peak coordinates for such contrasts. Therefore it fails the critical inclusion criterion requiring clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4) and the requirements for whole-brain, coordinate-based bvFTD-versus-control results (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria from the review list are triggered. Consequently the paper must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not use voxelwise whole-brain neuroimaging modalities or report voxelwise peak coordinates required by the review. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (results are region-level/ROI volumetric analyses—lobar and hippocampal volumes and percentiles—with no unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise analyses or reported peak MNI/Talairach coordinates). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (patient group size criteria: FTD group n=15, which is >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is automated regional volumetry/segmentation, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I4 (paper reports FTD but does not specify behavioral variant FTD/bvFTD or Pick's disease explicitly), I6 (no between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample), I8 (no peak coordinates reported). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This is an FDG-PET study with a suitable patient sample size but it does not report the required whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts with peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I5 (patient group N=14 FTD ≥6; control group N=33 ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported between-group bvFTD-versus-control contrast in defined stereotactic space), I7 (no clearly reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise result identified for bvFTD group), I8 (no peak coordinates reported for bvFTD-versus-control contrasts). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded from the coordinate-based meta-analysis focused on bvFTD.

Although the study used VBM (FSL-VBM) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with sufficient sample sizes, it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise bvFTD-versus-control contrasts with peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. The MRI analysis extracted regional volumes from an a priori subset of atlas-defined regions and the reported results focus on region-level volumes and classification performance rather than whole-brain statistical maps or peak coordinates. Therefore the qualifying results are effectively ROI-based and no unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise contrast with coordinates is provided. Exclusion applied: E6 (qualifying result comes from region-of-interest analysis and no unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise result reported). Inclusions met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD present), I5 (≥6 participants per patient/control group). Inclusions not met: I6, I7, I8 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrast in standard space, no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result for bvFTD, and no peak coordinates provided). Full text appears complete.

While this study used voxel-based morphometry (I3) and includes an adequate FTD patient group (n=8) and controls (n=26) meeting minimum sample sizes (I5), it does not meet several required inclusion criteria for this review. The paper does not specify that the FTD cases are behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) rather than other FTD subtypes (I4 not met/uncertain). Crucially, the study does not report any whole-brain, group-level bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise contrasts with peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. The coordinates provided (e.g., 10, 22, -20) pertain to within-FTD comparisons (ϵ4 carriers vs non-carriers) rather than a bvFTD vs control contrast, so I6, I7, and I8 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria E5–E9 are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to report a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast with peak coordinates and for not clearly identifying the sample as bvFTD.

Exclusion: E6 applies – the study reports hippocampal volumetry and a visual MTA rating (region-of-interest/ROI measures) and does not report any unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (sample sizes meet minimum: FTLD n=42, controls n=73). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is structural hippocampal volumetry/MTA, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I4 (paper reports ‘frontotemporal dementia (FTD)’ but does not explicitly state behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease as the target diagnosis), I6 (no between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast for bvFTD vs controls reported), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results from target bvFTD sample), I8 (no peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded.

Although this study uses VBM (I3 satisfied), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (58 patients) (I4 satisfied), and has adequate sample sizes for patients and controls (I5 satisfied), it does NOT report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts of bvFTD versus controls with peak coordinates in MNI or Talairach space. The neuroimaging results are brain–behavior (VBM) correlations across a heterogeneous NDG sample and secondary error checks, not a bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise contrast with reported peak coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I8 are not met. No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not provide the necessary bvFTD-specific whole-brain coordinate results required for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses Voxel-Based Morphometry) and I5 (imaging subgroup includes >=6 patients and 27 controls for the overall FTLD vs control comparison). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the sample is described as FTLD with subgroups; the paper does not explicitly report a clinically diagnosed bvFTD/bvFTD-only group contrast), I6 (no clear between-group contrast reported that compares a bvFTD-only group to controls without pooling with other patient groups), I7 (no clearly identified whole-brain voxelwise result originating from a bvFTD-only target sample), I8 (no peak coordinates (x,y,z) in MNI/Talairach space are provided for a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were directly triggered. Note: a small subgroup analysis reported a disinhibited subgroup of n=4 (<6), which would not meet the sample-size requirement if that subgroup were considered the target; however, the principal reason for exclusion is missing bvFTD-specific whole-brain coordinates and contrasts.

Excluded because imaging and analysis do not meet the review's imaging and whole-brain/coordinate requirements. The study uses structural MRI lobar volumetry (region-of-interest/bilateral lobar volumes via BRAINS2) rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). No whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts or peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space are reported (fails I6, I7, I8). The patient sample size criterion is met (44 FTD patients; I5), and participants are clinically diagnosed FTD with exclusion of SD/PPA, consistent with bvFTD clinical sampling (I4). Because the reported results are ROI-based lobar volumes and no unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise coordinates are provided, exclusion criterion E6 applies (ROI-only results with no whole-brain voxelwise contrasts). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, multicenter study using structural MRI (VBM) and resting-state fMRI with clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and adequate sample sizes. It reports whole-brain VBM analyses comparing bvFTD to controls. However, the provided full text does not include any peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach) for bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrasts, and I8 (reporting actual peak coordinates) is not satisfied. Therefore the study cannot be included per the review’s coordinate-reporting requirement. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (core sections present).

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria and meets exclusion criteria. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (results are ROI/region-based volumetric and cortical-thickness comparisons rather than unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise analyses) and E9 (primary imaging analyses are cortical thickness/volumetric FreeSurfer methods, which the review excludes). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is structural MRI volumetrics/cortical thickness using FreeSurfer, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET), I4 (the paper reports an FTD group but does not specify clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease), I6 (no between‑group voxelwise contrasts in standard stereotaxic space reported), I7 (no group-level whole‑brain voxelwise result identified for bvFTD), I8 (no peak coordinates in MNI or Talairach space reported). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). The lack of voxelwise MNI/Talairach coordinates and use of surface/ROI volumetrics prevent inclusion in the coordinate-based meta-analysis targeting bvFTD voxelwise studies.

This study meets I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), and I5 (>=6 patients and >=6 controls). However, it does NOT report any bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast or peak coordinates. The neuroimaging results are within the combined FTD sample correlating atrophy with happiness behavior, not a group-level whole-brain contrast of bvFTD vs controls. Therefore inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I8 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet critical inclusion criteria for this review. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I5 (FTD patient group n=7 >=6), and I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise SPM group results for the FTD group vs controls are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the patient group is described as ‘FTD’ but the paper does not specify behavioral-variant FTD/bvFTD or Pick’s disease specifically), I6 (the target sample for this review must be a bvFTD group; the reported between-group contrasts are for an unspecified FTD group, not explicitly bvFTD), and I8 (the provided full text does not contain any peak coordinates in MNI or Talairach space for the FTD-versus-control contrast; Tables are referenced but coordinates are not presented in the text supplied). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Based solely on the provided full text, the study cannot be included because it fails to demonstrate that the patient group is bvFTD and does not report peak coordinates required for coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This is an empirical FTD case series (n=72) but does not meet key imaging and reporting inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Imaging modalities used were SPECT and structural MRI (not VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET) so I3 is not met. The paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise bvFTD‑vs‑control contrasts nor peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (I6, I7, and I8 are not met). The sample size criterion is satisfied (I5 met) and the sample consists of clinically diagnosed FTD patients with prominent behavioral features (interpretable as bvFTD; I4 applied), but the lack of an eligible imaging modality and absence of whole‑brain coordinate results precludes inclusion. Full text appears complete. Exclusion criteria: none applicable.

The study is excluded because it reports ROI-based metabolic connectivity analyses using AAL parcellation (regional/VOI analyses) rather than whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and does not provide peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTLD patients: 35 behavioral-variant cases), I5 (patient and control groups ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no voxelwise bvFTD-versus-control contrast reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from bvFTD group), I8 (no peak coordinates reported). Applicable exclusion criteria: E6 (qualifying results come from region-of-interest/atlas-parcellation analyses, not unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Full text is a behavioral/actigraphy study of sleep in bvFTD and does not use any of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). It therefore fails inclusion criterion I3. The paper does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=13) and control groups (≥6), satisfying I4 and I5. However, it reports no between-group whole-brain voxelwise neuroimaging contrasts, no group-level whole-brain results in MNI/Talairach space, and provides no peak coordinates—failing I6, I7, and I8. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because neuroimaging-specific inclusion criteria (I3, I6, I7, I8) are not met.

This is a clinical case series of a family with a progranulin (PGRN) mutation using structural MRI and neuropsychological/neuropathological data. It does not use VBM, fMRI (task or resting), or FDG-PET (I3 not met). Although the sample includes individuals clinically diagnosed with frontotemporal dementia/FTLD (some with behavioural features) satisfying I4, the study does not report any whole-brain voxelwise group analyses comparing a bvFTD group to controls, nor does it provide peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (I6, I7, I8 not met). The imaging sample that underwent MRI is small (4 patients imaged) and no between-group voxelwise contrasts are reported, so I5 is not satisfied for the neuroimaging comparisons required by the review. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion requirements for the bvFTD meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM was used) and I5 (patient group sizes ≥6: FTD n=9, controls n=10). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (patients are reported as FTD but not specified as behavioral-variant FTD / Pick's disease), I6 (no between-group contrast reported comparing a bvFTD group to controls — bvFTD group is not separable or analyzed), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result identified for a bvFTD group), and I8 (no peak coordinates reported for any bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast). No exclusion criteria from the provided list were directly triggered. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because the review requires bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrasts with coordinates, this paper must be excluded.

The study meets several inclusion criteria: it uses VBM (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=7) (I4), the bvFTD and control groups exceed the minimum sample size (I5), it reports between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrasts for phenotypes including bvFTD versus controls (I6), and it provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results identified for the bvFTD phenotype (I7). However, the full text does not report any peak coordinates (x,y,z) in MNI/Talairach space for a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast (I8 not met). Because I8 is mandatory, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study uses VBM (satisfies I3), includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s patients (I4), and has adequate sample sizes for patients and controls (I5). However it does NOT report a between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast of bvFTD versus controls (I6 not met), does not present a whole-brain group-level bvFTD-versus-control result (I7 not met), and does not report peak coordinates for any bvFTD-versus-control contrast (I8 not met). The reported VBM result is a correlation across FTLD subjects (vertical saccade velocity correlated with dorsal midbrain volume) with MNI coordinates, but this is not a bvFTD-versus-control contrast. Therefore the paper fails required inclusion criteria I6–I8 and must be excluded.

The study uses FDG-PET (I3), includes an FTLD patient group of n=13 and control group n=10 meeting sample size requirements (I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons (I7). However, the patient group is described as frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) without specification that cases are clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease, so I4 is not satisfied. The paper does not report any peak coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for FTLD-versus-control contrasts, so I8 is not satisfied. Consequently, the required between-group contrast specifically for bvFTD (I6/I4) is not available. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I4 and I8 (and thus I6 for a bvFTD-specific contrast). Exclusion criteria met: none specifically; exclusion applied: [].

The study uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD patients consistent with bvFTD (I4), has adequate sample sizes (98 FTD, 110 controls) meeting I5, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise comparisons of FTD versus controls in Talairach space (I6,I7). However, the full text does not report any peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach) for FTD-versus-control contrasts (I8 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to provide the required stereotactic peak coordinates (I8).

The study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging and whole-brain reporting criteria. Although it includes clinically diagnosed FTD cases (likely behavioral-variant FTD) and the patient group sizes meet the minimum (I4 and I5 are satisfied), the imaging was manual region-of-interest volumetry rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET (I3 not met). The paper does not report any whole‑brain, voxelwise bvFTD-versus-control contrasts nor peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (I6, I7, I8 not met). This qualifies as an ROI-based analysis with no unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise results, triggering exclusion criterion E6. Therefore the study cannot be included for the meta-analysis objective.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses FDG‑PET with voxelwise SPM analysis (I3); the patient sample consists of 29 clinically diagnosed FTD patients restricted to the behavioral-variant FTD phenotype (progressive nonfluent aphasia and semantic dementia were excluded, and clinical features described match bvFTD) (I4); sample sizes meet thresholds (29 patients, 11 controls) (I5); it reports a between-group voxelwise contrast of FTD versus controls in standardized space (images normalized to the MNI template and group SPM results reported) (I6,I7); and peak coordinates are provided (local maxima converted to Talairach coordinates listed in Table 3) (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (whole-brain voxelwise results reported; not a review; not ROI-only). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD patients included; n=28), I5 (bvFTD group and control group sizes >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7, I8 — the paper does not report any between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast of bvFTD versus controls (results are voxelwise regressions across a mixed diagnostic sample tied to discrepancy scores), and no peak coordinates are provided for a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast in MNI/Talairach space. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because imaging modality and reported results do not meet the review’s imaging and coordinate-based whole-brain criteria. Although the study includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia (FD, i.e., bvFTD) patients (I4) and adequate sample sizes (I5: FD n=18, FTLD n=59, controls n=26), it uses structural MRI visual atrophy ratings rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). It does not report any voxelwise whole-brain group contrasts or peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (fails I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Therefore the paper must be excluded.

This study reports a whole-brain, voxelwise 18F-FDG PET analysis comparing clinically diagnosed FTD patients (29) to healthy controls (16). The paper used SPM voxelwise group comparisons with results reported in Talairach coordinates (e.g., x/y/z 10/27/30 and −36/39/4) and describes significant bilateral frontal hypometabolism in patients. Sample size meets the minimum (≥6 per group). The diagnosis excluded semantic dementia and non-fluent aphasia, indicating the sample represents behavioural-variant FTD (FTD clinical sample) rather than other FTLD variants. Although a subsequent regression was performed within an ROI, the primary group contrast is an unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise analysis with peak coordinates provided, satisfying whole-brain coordinate reporting. Full text content (methods, results, discussion, coordinates) is present and sufficient for screening.

This study is excluded because it does not report the required whole‑brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts with peak coordinates for a bvFTD (behavioral/social/dysexecutive) patient group versus controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (used VBM), I4 (included a social/dysexecutive [SOC/EXEC] FTLD subgroup consistent with bvFTD, n=17), I5 (patient subgroup and control group sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no clear report of a between-group voxelwise contrast of bvFTD/SOC/EXEC versus controls separate from other patient groups), I7 (no presented group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD/SOC/EXEC sample), I8 (no peak coordinates [MNI/Talairach x,y,z] reported for any bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast). Exclusion criteria met: none of the listed exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply based on the available full text.

The study uses FDG-PET and reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with reported peak coordinates (supplementary table E-1), and has adequate sample sizes (FTD n=29, FTD/MND n=8, controls n=11). However, the paper reports participants as having frontotemporal dementia (FTD) per Neary criteria but does not explicitly label the patient group as behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease, nor does it provide a clear breakdown that allows confirmation that the bvFTD diagnosis was the target group in the reported bvFTD-versus-control contrasts. Because inclusion criterion I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease patients) is not verifiably met, the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This study should be excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the bvFTD coordinate-based meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET was used) and I5 (patient and control group sizes exceed 6 overall: FTD total n≈31 and controls per scanner n≥20). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the paper reports FTD but does not explicitly specify behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast reported specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space), I7 (no clearly identified group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from a bvFTD sample is reported), and I8 (no peak coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast are provided). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study cannot be included for the coordinate-based bvFTD meta-analysis.

While this study reports voxel-wise structural MRI atrophy maps (VBM-like) and provides peak coordinates and adequate group sizes, it does not include a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) or Pick’s disease patient group nor report a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast. This FDG-PET study addresses FTLD and includes a behavioral-variant FTD (FTD) subgroup and healthy controls, and it reports voxelwise whole-brain SPM group contrasts (FTD vs controls). It therefore meets I3 (FDG-PET modality), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed FTD cases), I5 (bvFTD subgroup size n≈6 and controls n=9 meet the ≥6 requirement), I6 (reports between-group voxelwise contrasts of FTD versus controls), and I7 (provides whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). Because inclusion criterion I8 (reporting of peak coordinates) is not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered by the content. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results and discussion, but peak coordinates are absent in the supplied text, so I8 is unmet.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to perform whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons between patient subgroups and healthy controls and reports peak-voxel summaries (the text states that peak voxels are summarized in tables and coordinates were transformed to Talairach space). The SOC/EXEC subgroup is described as nonaphasic FTD patients with a disorder of social comportment and executive processing, which corresponds to behavioral-variant FTD-like presentation. The SOC/EXEC group contains sufficient participants at the clinical-sample level (32 total; imaging subset described as including all patient groups and matched), and group-level two-sample t-tests comparing each patient group to controls are reported. Thus the paper meets the imaging modality (I3), includes a bvFTD-like subgroup (I4), has sufficient sample sizes (I5), reports between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard space (I6), provides whole-brain voxelwise results for patient groups (I7), and indicates peak-voxel reporting (I8). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3). It includes a distinct social/executive (SOC/EXEC) FTLD subgroup characterized by social disinhibition, apathy, and executive deficits that corresponds to behavioral-variant FTD features (bvFTD) (I4). The SOC/EXEC group has 12 patients (I5) and controls are reported (n=10). The paper reports subgroup-wise whole-brain VBM contrasts versus controls using SPM5 (two-sample t-tests) and identifies significant atrophy clusters for the SOC/EXEC subgroup (I6,I7). The text states that the anatomic loci of peak clusters are summarized in Table 4, indicating reported peak coordinates for the subgroup contrasts (I8). There is no indication of exclusion criteria being met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, appendices). Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria for bvFTD-related whole-brain VBM results and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This grant-report article does not present any empirically reported whole-brain voxelwise bvFTD-versus-control contrasts with peak coordinates. While the project aims include differentiating bvFTD from AD/NC, the specific studies summarized focus on structural MRI subfield shape (PPA, AD, mutation carriers), FDG-PET analyses of AD/ MCI progression using ADNI, and machine-learning classification across AD/FTD subtypes. No section reports a clinically diagnosed bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) patient group compared against controls with whole-brain voxelwise results and peak (x,y,z) coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore only inclusion criterion I3 (use of FDG-PET/structural MRI modalities) is satisfied. Inclusion criteria I4 (bvFTD sample), I5 (>=6 bvFTD patients in reported contrast), I6 (between-group contrast in defined stereotaxic space for bvFTD vs controls), I7 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise result from target bvFTD sample), and I8 (reported peak coordinates for bvFTD-vs-control contrast) are not met. No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E5–E9) directly apply. Full text appears complete.
